transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

To be honest, I'm really only here because my mom and my manager were getting worried about me. I go from feeling like I can work nonstop and take on everything to suddenly having no energy to even show up for my shifts.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable—more than just feeling happy or excited?

Yes, I definitely experience those highs. I'll feel like I'm on top of the world, cracking jokes and running on this endless engine where I just can't sit still. But then a switch flips and I get incredibly irritable, snapping at my coworkers over tiny things like a messed-up ticket and I just can't seem to dial it back.
How long do these high or irritable periods usually last—do they last for several days or longer, and have you ever had a time when the high lasted a week or more?

Yeah, that high, energetic period lasted for about a whole month before I suddenly crashed. The entire back-and-forth has been going on for about four months now, and this current low, heavy feeling has been dragging me down for the last three months.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["F31", "F32", "F43.2"], but based on this conversation, F32 (depressive episode) and F43.2 (adjustment disorder) are less likely because the patient describes a distinct month-long period of elevated energy, reduced need for sleep, irritability, and increased activity, followed by a prolonged depressive episode lasting three months. This clear cycling between mania and depression over several months meets criteria for bipolar disorder (F31), whereas F32 and F43.2 do not account for manic episodes. The duration and pattern strongly support F31 as the most appropriate category.
